            'Store', 'Load', 'Line', 'Transformer' and'Link'.
        groupby_method : Callable | str, default="sum"
            Function to aggregate groups when using the groupby parameter.
            Any pandas aggregation function can be used.
        aggregate_across_components : bool, default=False
            Whether to aggregate across components. If there are different 
components
            which would be grouped together due to the same index, this is 
avoided.
        groupby : str | Sequence[str] | Callable, default="carrier"
            How to group components:
            - `False`: No grouping, return all components individually
            - string or list of strings: Group by column names from 
[c.static][pypsa.Components]
            - callable: Function that takes network and component name as 
arguments
        at_port : PortsLike, default="bus0"
            Which ports to consider:
            - "all": All ports of components
            - "bus0": Consider only first port
            - str or list of str: Specific ports to include (e.g., "bus1", 
"bus2")
        carrier : str | Sequence[str] | None, default=None
            Filter by carrier. If specified, only considers assets with given
            carrier(s).
        bus_carrier : str | Sequence[str] | None, default=None
            Filter by carrier of connected buses. If specified, only considers 
assets
            connected to buses with the given carrier(s).
        nice_names : bool | None, default=None
            Whether to use carrier nice names defined in n.carriers.nice_name. 
Defaults
            to module wide option (default: True).
            See `https://go.pypsa.org/options-params` for more information.
        drop_zero : bool | None, default=None
            Whether to drop zero values from the result. Defaults to module wide
option
            (default: True). See `https://go.pypsa.org/options-params` for more 
information.
        round : int | None, default=None
            Number of decimal places to round the result to. Defaults to module 
wide
            option (default: 2). See `https://go.pypsa.org/options-params` for 
more information.

        Other Parameters
        ----------------
        groupby_time : str | bool, default="sum"
            Type of aggregation when aggregating time series. Deactivate by 
setting to
            False. Any pandas aggregation function can be used. Note that when
            aggregating the time series are aggregated to MWh using snapshot 
weightings.
            With False the time series is given in MW.

        Returns
        -------
        pd.DataFrame
            Transmission of branch components in the network with components as 
rows and
            either time steps as columns (if groupby_time=False) or a single 
column
            of aggregated values.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> n.statistics.transmission()
        Series([], dtype: object)

        """
        n = self._n

        if components is None:
            components = n.branch_components

        transmission_branches = get_transmission_branches(n, bus_carrier)

        @pass_empty_series_if_keyerror
        def func(n: Network, c: str, port: str) -> pd.Series:
            idx = transmission_branches.get_loc_level(c, level="component")[1]
            p = n.c[c].dynamic[f"p{port}"][idx]
            weights = n.snapshot_weightings.generators
            return self._aggregate_timeseries(p, weights, agg=groupby_time)

        df = self._aggregate_components(
            func,
            components=components,
            agg=groupby_method,
            aggregate_across_components=aggregate_across_components,
            groupby=groupby,
            at_port=at_port,
            carrier=carrier,
            bus_carrier=bus_carrier,
            nice_names=nice_names,
            drop_zero=drop_zero,
            round=round,
        )
        df.attrs["name"] = "Transmission"
        df.attrs["unit"] = "carrier dependent"
        return df

linopy.options["semantics"] = sys.argv[1]

    def reindex(
        self,
        indexers: Mapping[Any, Any] | None = None,
        *,
        method: str | None = None,
        tolerance: Any = None,
        copy: bool = True,
        fill_value: Any = FILL_VALUE,
        **indexers_kwargs: Any,
    ) -> LinearExpression:
        """
        Conform to new coordinates as ``Dataset.reindex``. For a CSR-backed
        expression, returns a CSR-backed result when only grid labels change
        and no other keyword argument is given.
        """
        indexers = either_dict_or_kwargs(indexers, indexers_kwargs, "reindex")
        csr = self._csr
        if (
            csr is not None
            and set(indexers) <= set(csr.grid.dims)
            and method is None
            and tolerance is None
            and copy
            and fill_value is self._fill_value
        ):
            grid = csr.grid.with_indexes(indexers)
            return type(self)._from_csr(csr.reindexed(grid), self._model)
        return super().reindex(
            indexers,
            method=method,
            tolerance=tolerance,
            copy=copy,
            fill_value=fill_value,
        )

def rep(old,new,count=1):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==count, (s.count(old), old)
    s=s.replace(old,new)

_leading_dim(expr: LinearExpression, dim: str) -> LinearExpression:
    """Make `dim` the first dimension of `expr`."""
    if expr.dims[0] == dim:
        return expr
    return LinearExpression(expr.data.transpose(dim, ...), expr.model)

    def _from_csr(cls, csr: CSRLinearExpression, model: Model) -> Self:
        """Construct an expression backed by a CSRLinearExpression."""
        obj = cls.__new__(cls)
        obj._model = model
        obj._data = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
        obj._csr = csr
        return obj

    @property
    def data(self) -> Dataset:
        self._densify("`.data` read, e.g. by an operation without a sparse 
path")
        return self._data

    def _densify(self, reason: str) -> None:
        """Convert the CSR backing to dense for good, with a notice naming 
``reason``."""
        _densify_all([self], reason)

    @property
    def is_sparse(self) -> bool:
        """
        Whether the expression is backed by a sparse CSR matrix
        (:mod:`linopy.csr`) instead of a dense Dataset. Reading ``.data``, or
        an operation without a sparse path, converts it to dense for good.
        """
        return self._csr is not None

    @property
    def coord_dims(self) -> tuple[Hashable, ...]:
        if self._csr is not None:
            return self._csr.grid.dims
        return super().coord_dims

$ cd /app/pypsa && python - <<'EOF'
p='pypsa/optimization/expressions.py'
s=open(p).read()
old='''def _leading_dim(expr: LinearExpression, dim: str) -> LinearExpression:
    """Make `dim` the first dimension of `expr`."""
    if expr.dims[0] == dim:
        return expr
    return LinearExpression(expr.data.transpose(dim, ...), expr.model)
'''
new='''def _leading_dim(expr: LinearExpression, dim: str) -> LinearExpression:
    """Make `dim` the first dimension of `expr`.

    The dimension order of linopy expressions follows the order of their 
coordinates.
    """
    if expr.dims[0] == dim:
        return expr
    data = expr.data
    coords = data.coords
    names = [k for k, c in coords.items() if dim in c.dims]
    names += [k for k, c in coords.items() if dim not in c.dims]
    ordered = Coordinates(
        {k: coords[k].variable for k in names}, indexes=dict(data.xindexes)
    )
    variables = {k: v.variable.transpose(dim, ...) for k, v in 
data.data_vars.items()}
    return LinearExpression(Dataset(coords=ordered).assign(variables), 
expr.model)
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

def test_grouping_by_new_registered_key(ac_dc_network_r):
    def new_grouper(n, c):
        return n.c[c].static.index.to_series()

    n = ac_dc_network_r
    pypsa.statistics.groupers.add_grouper("new_grouper", new_grouper)
    df = n.statistics.supply(groupby="new_grouper")
    assert not df.empty
    assert df.index.nlevels == 2

    df = n.statistics.supply(groupby=["new_grouper", "carrier"], 
components="Link")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not supported"):
        n.statistics.prices(groupby="not_an_attribute")

def _capacities_mw(n: pypsa.Network):
    # A quick helper to return installed capacities as MW Series indexed by 
(component, carrier) for almost_equal check
    cap = n.statistics.optimal_capacity()
    if "scenario" in cap.index.names:
        without_scen = [lvl for lvl in cap.index.names if lvl != "scenario"]
        cap = cap.groupby(level=without_scen).first()
    cap = cap.groupby(level=["component", "carrier"]).sum()
    return cap.sort_index()


def _objective_bil(n: pypsa.Network) -> float:
    assert n.objective is not None
    return n.objective / 1e9

Reasoning:
The objectives match, but the storage dispatch differs in mp_stochastic, 
including between the two legacy formulations that should have identical 
semantics. That points toward degenerate solutions with zero-cost storage 
operations, where the LP picks a different optimal vertex depending on variable 
and constraint ordering. Since legacy-flat and legacy-multiindex differ despite 
the same semantics, ordering seems the likely cause, but I still want to check 
whether this is really degeneracy or a genuine formulation difference.

I'll check whether the two formulations really match by canonicalizing each LP: 
for every constraint row I'd compare the sorted coefficient tuples, sign and 
right-hand side, with variables mapped to their name and coordinates. Flattened 
snapshot keys need normalizing so they line up with the multi-index version. 
That should catch any silent semantic differences beyond the objective.

Storage dispatch differences in the stochastic multi-period case look like 
degenerate optima rather than formulation differences, so I'm diffing the 
canonicalised LP constraints and variable bounds between modes to confirm.

    """Build models under given semantics and dump a canonical LP 
representation.
    
    usage: python lpcanon.py <semantics> <snapshot_index_option> <out.pkl> 
[networks]
    """
    
    import pickle
    import sys
    import warnings
    from collections import Counter
    
    import linopy
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd
    
    import pypsa
    
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
    import logging
    
    logging.disable(logging.WARNING)
    
    sem, opt, out = sys.argv[1:4]
    only = sys.argv[4].split(",") if len(sys.argv) > 4 else None
    linopy.options["semantics"] = sem
    pypsa.options.optimization.model_snapshot_index = opt
    pypsa.options.params.optimize.include_objective_constant = False
    
    src = open("/tmp/harness.py").read()
    exec(src[src.index("def multi_period():") : src.index("STATS = ")])
    
    
    def flat_key(values):
        key = []
        for v in values:
            if isinstance(v, tuple):
                key.extend(v)
            else:
                key.append(v)
        return tuple(str(k) for k in key)
    
    
    def canon(m):
        labelmap = {}
        bounds = Counter()
        for name, var in m.variables.items():
            labels = var.labels
            df = labels.to_dataframe("label").reset_index()
            coords = [c for c in df.columns if c not in ("label",) and c in 
labels.dims]
            lower = var.lower.broadcast_like(labels).values.ravel()
            upper = var.upper.broadcast_like(labels).values.ravel()
            lab = labels.values.ravel()
            idx = df[coords].to_numpy() if coords else np.empty((len(df), 0))
            for i, (l, row) in enumerate(zip(df["label"].to_numpy(), idx)):
                if l == -1:
                    continue
                labelmap[l] = (name, flat_key(row))
            for l, lo, up, row in zip(lab, lower, upper, idx):
                if l != -1:
                    bounds[(name, flat_key(row), round(float(lo), 6), 
round(float(up), 6))] += 1
        rows = Counter()
        for name, con in m.constraints.items():
            flat = con.flat
            if flat.empty:
                continue
            for label, g in flat.groupby("labels"):
                terms = Counter()
                for v, c in zip(g["vars"], g["coeffs"]):
                    if v == -1:
                        continue
                    terms[labelmap[v]] += c
                terms = tuple(sorted((k, round(c, 6)) for k, c in terms.items() 
if abs(c) > 1e-12))
                rows[(name, terms, g["sign"].iloc[0], 
round(float(g["rhs"].iloc[0]), 6))] += 1
        obj = Counter()
        of = m.objective.flat
        for v, c in zip(of["vars"], of["coeffs"]):
            if v != -1:
                obj[labelmap[v]] += c
        obj = {k: round(c, 6) for k, c in obj.items() if abs(c) > 1e-12}
        return {"rows": rows, "bounds": bounds, "obj": obj}
    
    
    res = {}
    for key, make in NETWORKS.items():
        if only and key not in only:
            continue
        try:
            n, kw = make()
            if key == "model_energy":
                n.set_snapshots(n.snapshots[:50])
            kw = {k: v for k, v in kw.items()}
            n.optimize.create_model(**kw)
            res[key] = canon(n.model)
        except Exception as e:
            import traceback
    
            res[key] = traceback.format_exc()
    pickle.dump(res, open(out, "wb"))
    print("saved")

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd
    
    sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp")
    
    RECORDS = {}
    COUNTS = defaultdict(int)
    MAX_ROWS = 30000
    
    
    def flat_key(values):
        key = []
        for v in values:
            if isinstance(v, tuple):
                key.extend(v)
            else:
                key.append(v)
        return tuple(str(k) for k in key)
    
    
    def canon(m):
        if m.constraints.ncons > MAX_ROWS:
            return "too large"
        labelmap = {}
        bounds = Counter()
        for name, var in m.variables.items():
            labels = var.labels
            df = labels.to_dataframe("label").reset_index()
            coords = []
            for d in labels.dims:
                index = labels.indexes.get(d)
                coords += list(index.names) if isinstance(index, pd.MultiIndex) 
else [d]
            lower = var.lower.broadcast_like(labels).values.ravel()
            upper = var.upper.broadcast_like(labels).values.ravel()
            lab = labels.values.ravel()
            idx = df[coords].to_numpy() if coords else np.empty((len(df), 0))
            for l, row in zip(df["label"].to_numpy(), idx):
                if l != -1:
                    labelmap[l] = (name, flat_key(row))
            for l, lo, up, row in zip(lab, lower, upper, idx):
                if l != -1:
                    bounds[(name, flat_key(row), round(float(lo), 5), 
round(float(up), 5))] += 1
        rows = Counter()
        for name, con in m.constraints.items():
            flat = con.flat
            if flat.empty:
                continue
            for _, g in flat.groupby("labels"):
                terms = Counter()
                for v, c in zip(g["vars"], g["coeffs"]):
                    if v != -1:
                        terms[labelmap[v]] += c
                terms = tuple(
                    sorted((k, round(c, 5)) for k, c in terms.items() if abs(c) 
> 1e-10)
                )
                rows[(name, terms, g["sign"].iloc[0], 
round(float(g["rhs"].iloc[0]), 5))] += 1
        obj = Counter()
        try:
            of = m.objective.flat
            for v, c in zip(of["vars"], of["coeffs"]):
                if v != -1:
                    obj[labelmap.get(v, v)] += c
        except Exception as e:  # quadratic etc.
            obj["error"] = str(e)[:50]
        obj = {k: round(c, 5) for k, c in obj.items() if not isinstance(c, 
float) or abs(c) > 1e-10}
        return {"rows": rows, "bounds": bounds, "obj": obj}
    
    
    def _record(tag, m):
        test = os.environ.get("PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST", "?").rsplit(" ", 1)[0]
        COUNTS[(test, tag)] += 1
        key = (test, tag, COUNTS[(test, tag)])
        try:
            RECORDS[key] = canon(m)
        except Exception as e:
            RECORDS[key] = f"canon error {type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
    
    
    def pytest_configure(config):
        from pypsa.optimization.optimize import OptimizationAccessor
    
        orig_create = OptimizationAccessor.create_model
    
        def create_model(self, *args, **kwargs):
            m = orig_create(self, *args, **kwargs)
            _record("create", m)
            return m
    
        OptimizationAccessor.create_model = create_model
        orig_solve = linopy.Model.solve
    
        def solve(self, *args, **kwargs):
            _record("solve", self)
            return orig_solve(self, *args, **kwargs)
    
        linopy.Model.solve = solve
    
    
    def pytest_unconfigure(config):
        worker = os.environ.get("PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER", "main")
        out = os.environ.get("LPPLUGIN_OUT", "/tmp/lprec")
        os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
        with open(f"{out}/{worker}.pkl", "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(RECORDS, f)

+@contextmanager
+def _flat_snapshots_context(n: Network, flat: bool = True) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Read snapshot-indexed component data of `n` with flat snapshots.
+
+    Within the context, `c.da` of all components of `n` labels multi-period
+    snapshots by ``(period, timestep)`` tuples, see `_flatten_snapshots`.

+    others = tuple(other for other in networks if other is not n)

+def _flat_snapshot_index(sns: pd.MultiIndex) -> pd.Index:
+    """Return the snapshots as a flat index labelled by ``(period, timestep)`` 
tuples."""
+    return pd.Index(sns.to_flat_index(), name="snapshot", tupleize_cols=False)
+
+
+def _flat_snapshot_coords(sns: pd.MultiIndex) -> xr.Coordinates:
+    """Build a flat ``snapshot`` coordinate with the levels as auxiliary 
coordinates."""
+    coords = {"snapshot": _flat_snapshot_index(sns)}
+    coords.update({lvl: ("snapshot", sns.get_level_values(lvl)) for lvl in 
sns.names})
+    return xr.Coordinates(coords)
+
+
+def _flatten_snapshots(obj: Any) -> Any:
+    """Replace a MultiIndex ``snapshot`` dimension by its flat representation.
+
+    Coordinate order is kept, with the former levels following ``snapshot``.
+    """
+    sns = obj.indexes.get("snapshot")
+    if not isinstance(sns, pd.MultiIndex):
+        return obj
+    levels = list(sns.names)
+    order = []
+    for name in obj.coords:
+        if name == "snapshot":
+            order += ["snapshot", *levels]
+        elif name not in levels:
+            order.append(name)
+    flat = obj.drop_vars(["snapshot", *levels]).assign_coords(
+        _flat_snapshot_coords(sns)
+    )
+    coords = xr.Coordinates(
+        {name: flat.coords[name].variable for name in order},
+        indexes=dict(flat.xindexes),
+    )
+    return flat.drop_vars(list(flat.coords)).assign_coords(coords)
+
+
+def _unflatten_snapshots(obj: Any, levels: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> Any:
+    """Restore a MultiIndex ``snapshot`` dimension from its flat 
representation.
+
+    Levels are taken from the auxiliary snapshot coordinates, or from 
``levels``
+    if those are missing.
+    """
+    sns = obj.indexes.get("snapshot")
+    if sns is None or isinstance(sns, pd.MultiIndex) or sns.dtype != object:
+        return obj
+    if not len(sns) or not all(isinstance(s, tuple) for s in sns):
+        return obj
+    aux = [
+        name
+        for name, coord in obj.coords.items()
+        if name != "snapshot" and coord.dims == ("snapshot",)
+    ]
+    names = aux if aux else list(levels or [])
+    if len(names) != len(sns[0]):
+        return obj
+    multi = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(sns, names=names)
+    multi.name = "snapshot"
+    restored = obj.drop_vars(["snapshot", *aux])
+    return restored.assign_coords(
+        xr.Coordinates.from_pandas_multiindex(multi, "snapshot")
+    )
+

+def _model_is_flat(m: Model) -> bool:
+    """Whether the model labels multi-period snapshots by a flat index."""
+    if "snapshots" not in m.parameters:
+        return False
+    snapshots = m.parameters["snapshots"]
+    return "period" in snapshots.coords and not isinstance(
+        snapshots.indexes.get("snapshot"), pd.MultiIndex
+    )

+def _network_snapshots(n: Network, sns: pd.Index) -> pd.Index:
+    """Convert model snapshots back to the network's snapshot index."""
+    if isinstance(n.snapshots, pd.MultiIndex):
+        sns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(list(sns), names=n.snapshots.names)
+    sns.name = n.snapshots.name
+    return sns

+
+def _as_model_snapshots(n: Network, obj: Any) -> Any:
+    """Convert snapshot-indexed data to the snapshot representation of the 
model.
+
+    Supports snapshot indexes, pandas objects indexed by snapshots and xarray
+    objects with a snapshot dimension. Other objects are returned unchanged.
+    """
+    if not _model_is_flat(n.model):
+        return obj
+    if isinstance(obj, pd.MultiIndex):
+        return _flat_snapshot_index(obj)
+    if isinstance(obj, pd.Series | pd.DataFrame):
+        if isinstance(obj.index, pd.MultiIndex) and obj.index.names == list(
+            n.snapshots.names
+        ):
+            return obj.set_axis(_flat_snapshot_index(obj.index), axis=0)
+        return obj
+    if isinstance(obj, xr.DataArray | xr.Dataset):
+        return _flatten_snapshots(obj)
+    return obj
+

``group``

+    if not keys:
+        return expr
+    groups = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(
+        [expr.coords[key].values for key in keys], names=keys
+    )
+    return expr.drop_vars(["group", *keys]).assign_coords(
+        Coordinates.from_pandas_multiindex(groups, "group")
+    )

+def _leading_dim(expr: LinearExpression, dim: str) -> LinearExpression:
+    """Make `dim` the first dimension of `expr`.
+
+    The dimension order of linopy expressions follows the order of their 
coordinates.
+    """
+    if expr.dims[0] == dim:
+        return expr
+    data = expr.data
+    coords = data.coords
+    names = [k for k, c in coords.items() if dim in c.dims]
+    names += [k for k, c in coords.items() if dim not in c.dims]
+    ordered = Coordinates(
+        {k: coords[k].variable for k in names}, indexes=dict(data.xindexes)
+    )
+    variables = {k: v.variable.transpose(dim, ...) for k, v in 
data.data_vars.items()}
+    return LinearExpression(Dataset(coords=ordered).assign(variables), 
expr.model)
+
+
+def _sum_aligned(*exprs: Any) -> LinearExpression:
+    """Sum expressions over the union of their labels, absent labels count as 
zero."""
+    exprs_ = [e.to_linexpr() if isinstance(e, Variable) else e for e in exprs]
+    if len(exprs_) == 1:
+        return exprs_[0]
+    return ln.merge(exprs_, join="outer")
+

+def _capacity(n: Network, component: str, include_non_extendable: bool) -> Any:
+    """Capacity of extendable (variable) and non-extendable (constant) 
assets."""
+    m = n.model
+    c = n.c[component]
+    nom_attr = c._operational_attrs["nom"]
+    var_name = f"{component}-{nom_attr}"
+
+    non_ext_capacity = (
+        c.static.loc[c.fixed, nom_attr]
+        if include_non_extendable
+        else pd.Series(dtype=float)
+    )
+
+    if var_name in m.variables:
+        if non_ext_capacity.empty:
+            return m.variables[var_name].to_linexpr()
+        return _sum_aligned(
+            m.variables[var_name], LinearExpression.from_constant(m, 
non_ext_capacity)
+        )
+    if not non_ext_capacity.empty:
+        return LinearExpression.from_constant(m, non_ext_capacity)
+    return None

def test_statistics(ac_dc_stochastic_r):
    """
    Test the statistics of a stochastic network.
    """
    n = ac_dc_stochastic_r
    ds = n.statistics.installed_capacity()
    assert isinstance(ds, pd.Series)
    assert isinstance(ds.index, pd.MultiIndex)
    assert "scenario" in ds.index.names
    assert not ds.empty

    stats = n.statistics()
    assert isinstance(stats, pd.DataFrame)
    assert isinstance(stats.index, pd.MultiIndex)
    assert "scenario" in ds.index.names
    assert not stats.empty

    df = n.statistics.supply(groupby_time=False)

Message from Agent ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Multi-period networks (and the other cases you listed) now build, solve and 
report under linopy's v1 semantics with the same results as under legacy. The 
full test suite gives the same result under legacy, legacy with `flat` 
snapshots, and v1 with warnings treated as errors: 1706 passed in each, with the
same 6 failures/errors in all three that the original code also had (5 need 
network access, plus `test_io.py::test_version_warning`).

**The new option.** `pypsa.options.optimization.model_snapshot_index` takes 
`"auto"` (the default), `"multiindex"` or `"flat"`. It is resolved when a model 
is built, and any other value raises `ValueError` then. With `flat`, the model 
has a single `snapshot` dimension labelled by `(period, timestep)` tuples, 
followed by `period` and `timestep` coordinates. The model uses that 
representation throughout: `c.da` returns flat data while the model is built and
inside `extra_functionality`, and that callback receives flat snapshots. Outside
the model, `c.da` and the network keep the MultiIndex, and solutions and duals 
are written back with the network's own index.

**What broke under v1, besides the MultiIndex.** Most failures, single-period 
ones included, came from v1's stricter rules:
- **Label mismatches.** Arrays covering all assets were combined with variables 
covering only active assets or a subset of snapshots. These are now restricted 
to the same labels.
- **Absent entries spreading.** Shifted, masked or spill variables would have 
dropped constraint rows, for example the first-snapshot unit-commitment 
transitions and storage balances. They are now filled with zero, which is what 
legacy did.
- **Missing values.** Missing values in right-hand sides and cost coefficients 
now raise under v1; they are filled with 0, which is what legacy effectively 
did. Uneven piecewise curves now pass an explicit `mask`.

**How I checked "same results".** I compared the models themselves, not just 
objectives. I recorded every model built or solved in the optimisation tests 
(876 models) under legacy and v1 and compared each one constraint by constraint,
plus all variable bounds and objective coefficients. All are identical except 
one piecewise unit-commitment test. There legacy keeps three rows (`status ≥ 0`,
`delta ≥ 0`) that linopy's own piecewise code drops under v1; they are already 
implied by the variable bounds, so the problem is unchanged. On 13 networks (the
cached examples, snapshot subsets, multi-period with unit commitment, transport 
delays, stochastic) the objectives match. The only dispatch difference is 
storage in the stochastic multi-period case; that model is identical too, so it 
is a tie between equally good solutions.

**Expressions vs statistics.** The expressions keep their legacy output shape (a
MultiIndex `group` dimension), so existing code like `.unstack("group")` still 
works; I used linopy's `reindex_like` to keep that working under v1. Making them
agree with `n.statistics` meant fixing bugs that also exist under legacy, so 
these change legacy output too:
- **`transmission`:** it had the opposite sign to statistics, picked up stray 
`Line`/`Link` dimensions, and now defaults to `at_port="bus0"` like statistics.
- **`capex`, `capacity`, `curtailment`:** mixing extendable and fixed assets 
silently dropped the fixed ones (or lined them up by position); they are now 
combined properly.
- **Stores** now use their power (`p`) rather than their energy level.
- **Loads** are counted only over the modelled snapshots.
- **Multi-period** expressions now come out per period, matching the per-period 
statistics.
- **One component with `groupby=False`** used to crash and now returns per-asset
values.

**Other changes you might notice:**
- Some cross-component sums in global constraints now combine by label instead 
of by position, where legacy could wrongly line them up when the sizes happened 
to match.
- The primary-energy limit no longer crashes with "matrices are not aligned" 
when both continuous and per-period storages are present.
- `define_piecewise` now returns a `y_var` you pass in unchanged, so `result == 
y_var` comparisons work under v1.

**Not covered:**
- PyPSA doesn't read `LINOPY_SEMANTICS`; the tests (or the user) must set 
`linopy.options["semantics"]` themselves. I removed the temporary hook I'd added
to `test/conftest.py`.
- `n.optimize.expressions` still doesn't support stochastic networks; it already
failed there under legacy.
- Because expressions keep a MultiIndex `group`, they need 
`reset_index("group")` before going into `add_constraints` under v1.
- One existing bug is left alone: a period-specific primary-energy constraint 
combined with stores that reset each period still fails.
- No formatter was available, so I kept lines to black style by hand; `ruff 
format` might still make small changes.

All changes are in nine files under `/app/pypsa/pypsa`: `_options.py`, 
`components/array.py`, and `common.py`, `optimize.py`, `constraints.py`, 
`global_constraints.py`, `expressions.py`, `piecewise.py`, `mga.py` in 
`optimization/`.
